RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, December 2, 2010/Agrahayana 11, 1932 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Culture; External Af fairs;
Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation; Overseas Indian Affairs;
Parliamentary Affairs; Personnel, Public Grievances and
Pensions; Planning; Social Justice and Empowerment;
Space; Tourism; Urban Development; Water
Resources; Y outh Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
98
Reservation in private sector
*321. SHRI ISHWAR SINGH: Will
the  Minister  of  SOCIAL  JUSTICE
AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the National Commission
for Scheduled Castes has demanded 15 per
cent reservation for SCs in employment in
private sector;
(b) whether the Commission has
contended that since a large number of
private entrepreneurs avail loans from
public sector banks and financial
institutions and enjoy other incentives
and tax breaks, private sector should
reciprocate   this by providing employment
to SCs to the extent of 15 per cent;
and
(c) whether Government had earlier
broached the subject to private sector and
if so, the response thereto?
Release of water from Hathni Kund
Barrage
*322. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of W ATER RESOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Haryana
released huge quantity of water on many
occasions from Hathni Kund Barrage,
which caused floods in Yamuna river
deluging populated areas;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the reasons why water could not be
released in small, controlled and pre-
meditated quantities at intervals to prevent
floods in catchment areas;
(d) whether excessive and surplus water
in the overflowing rivers was stored for
water harvesting during lean period
anywhere in the country despite knowledge
of further monsoon rains, thereby resulting
in unprecedented flooding; and

99
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Nurturing of sports talent in the
country
*323. SHRI SHADI LAL BATRA: Will
the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND
SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the schemes
implemented by Sports Authority of India
(SAI) for spotting and nurturing of sports
talent in the country;
(b) the quantum of funds allocated and
expenditure incurred on sports promotion
during the last three years, State-wise,
sport-wise and year-wise; and
(c) the details of achievements made in
international sports during the last three
years?
Demand of houses in the country
*324. SHRI MOHAMMED AMIN:
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND
URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the present demand of housing in
the country, State-wise and low cost,
medium cost and high cost-wise;
(b) whether the demand can be met
within the next five years;
(c) whether there is any scheme to
provide low cost housing to construction
workers in all the States and UTs;
(d) the schemes meant for providing low
cost housing to urban poor people; and
(e) the details thereof?
CAG's findings in procurement by
nuclear plants
*325. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Comptroller and
Auditor General (CAG) has recently found
that 94 per cent of all procurements made
by nuclear plants were given out to a single
or limited vendors;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the CAG has asked the
Department of Atomic Energy to stop such
'secretive purchases'; and
(d) the steps that are being taken to
make the procurement process more fair
and transparent in the nuclear energy sector?
Maintenance of privacy in Unique
Identity Cards
†*326. SHRI UPENDRA
KUSHWAHA: W ill the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Unique
Identification Authority of India has been
established for making Unique Identity
Cards for people of the country;
(b) whether it is a fact that there would
be an expenditure of ` 45,000 crore on this
scheme during the next four years;
(c) whether it is also a fact that all private
information about the people in the said
identity card would become public, which
would be a violation of the fundamental
rights of the people; and
(d) if so, the arrangement being made to
maintain the privacy of individuals of the
country?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

100
Regularization of colonies in Delhi
*327. SHRI MOHAMMED ADEEB:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the colonies in Delhi
for whose regularization hurdles have been
cleared recently; and
(b) the steps being taken for speedy
development of such colonies?
Promotion of traditional folk art
forms
*328. SHRIMATI KANIMOZHI: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the steps taken by Government to
promote traditional folk art forms and
details thereof;
(b) total budgetary allocation for
promotion of folk art forms for the current
year; and
(c) whether this is only a small
proportion of the resources allocated for
contemporary arts and if so, the details
thereof?
RTI Cell in each Department
*329. SHRI VIJAY JAW AHARLAL
DARDA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Central Information
Commission has asked Government to
set up an RTI Cell in each Department and
appoint senior officials as Central Public
Information Officers;
(b) if so, whether these instructions have
been complied with; and
(c) if not, by when this exercise would
be completed so that the RTI Act is
comprehensively implemented to justify
the confidence being reposed by the general
public in this useful tool in their hands to
get information?
Impact of MGNREGA on small and
marginal farmers
*330. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Planning Commission has
completed any study or survey in last six
months on the impact of Mahatma Gandhi
National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
(MGNREGA) on small and marginal
farmers;
(b) whether this study has also been
done in Andhra Pradesh;
(c) if so, the findings of this study;
(d) whether additional inputs would be
directed to small and marginal farmers; and
(e) the details of new policies in this
regard to offset the neglect of farmers in
Eleventh Plan period?
Setting up of nuclear plants
*331. SHRI TARIQ ANW AR: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that four new
nuclear plants proposed to be set up have
not been cleared by the concerned body;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) the cities where the proposed nuclear
plants were to be set up; and
(d) the steps taken for their clearance?

101
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Indo-Chinese readiness for defence
exchanges
*332. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether both India and China have
expressed readiness to resume high-level
defence exchanges that have been put on
"pause" after a senior Indian army officer
was offered a stapled Chinese visa;
(b) if so, whether Prime Minister and
Chinese Premier discussed this issue on
the sidelines of East Asia Summit of Ten
Association of South East Asian Nations
(ASEAN) Members;
(c) if so, whether both Prime Ministers
have discussed and agreed to sort out the
issues relating to stapled visa and also
border talks; and
(d) if so, whether any date has been
fixed for resuming the talks with China on
these issues?
Allocation of funds to Maharashtra
*333. SHRI Y .P. TRIVEDI: Will the
Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:
(a) the amount which has been allocated
under Centrally sponsored schemes to the
State Government of Maharashtra during
financial years 2005-06 to 2009-10,
scheme-wise and year-wise;
(b) the amount released against this
allocation during the above mentioned
period, scheme-wise and year-wise; and
(c) the details of amount spent by the
State Government of Maharashtra, so far?
Nuclear plant in Fatehabad
†*334. SHRI SATYA VRAT
CHATURVEDI: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
the proposed nuclear power plant project
in Fatehabad district of Haryana is pending
due to non-availability of land;
(b) whether in view of opposition from
local farmers Government is taking any
steps for acquiring non-productive land for
this project elsewhere;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
National Sports Policy guidelines
*335. DR. PRABHAKAR KORE: Will
the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND
SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has initiated
action to modify the National Sports
Policy guidelines to infuse much-wanted
transparency and accountability in the
functioning of sports bodies;
(b) whether under the new guidelines,
there would  be a mandated upper age limit
for office-bearers and limiting the number
of terms of office;
(c) whether the new guidelines also
envisage bringing sports federations under
the purview of the RTI Act; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

102
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Indians facing racial violence
†*336. SHRI NARESH CHANDRA
AGRAWAL: W ill the Minister of
OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Indians living
in foreign countries, including Australia, are
facing racial and ethnic violence by local
people causing casualties to Indians;
(b) if so, the details of the discussion
between Indian Government and the
Governments of those countries along with
the outcome thereof;
(c) whether Government would
consider breaking all diplomatic ties with
these countries if such incidents recur; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Opening of Sanskriti schools
across the country
†*337. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has sanctioned
the action plan for opening Sanskriti schools
throughout the country in compliance with
court orders and whether admission of
wards of staff of All India Services/Central
Government would be ensured in these
schools; and
(b) the latest update in this regard and
the places where such schools are proposed
to be opened?
Rural urban divide
*338. DR. GY AN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) the statistics pertaining to the gap
between rural and urban sector, State-wise;
(b) the comparison of various
parameters, namely, education, health,
Maternal Mortality Rate, Infant Mortality
Rate, electricity, drinking water, roads,
teledensity, infrastructure, housing,
sanitation, contribution of GDP, per capita
annual income, etc.;
(c) the scenario of this gap in 2004 and
what it is at present;
(d) whether the gap is widening day by
day; and
(e) the plans being visualized to bridge
this ever widening gap?
Meeting with Chinese and Russian
Foreign Ministers
*339. SHRIMATI GUNDU
SUDHARANI: Will the Minister of
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Minister has met his
counterpart of China and Russia at Wuhan
during 14-15 November, 2010;
(b) whether the issue of Chinese
Government run mapping service showing
Arunachal Pradesh as a part of China has
come up for discussion;
(c) if so, the reaction from Chinese side;
(d) whether any assurance has been
given by Chinese Government to rectify
the mistake; and

103
NEW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 26th November, 2010 Secretary-General.
Agrahayana 5, 1932 (Saka)
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Issuing of UID numbers
*340. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Unique Identification
Authorityof India (UIDAI) has started the
process of issuing unique identification
numbers to citizens;
(b) the purpose behind issuing unique
identification numbers to all citizens;
(c) the numbers of UIDs that would be
issued over the next five years and the
estimated cost of the same;
(d) whether such identification
numbers would be made mandatory for
all citizens;
(e) whether such identification numbers
would be made mandatory for access to
Government schemes/programmes; and
(f) if so, Government schemes/
programmes where UID would be
mandatory?

104
I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Prime Minister :—
Atomic Energy : 325, 331, 334,
Culture : 328,
External Affairs : 332, 339,
Housing and Urban Poverty
Alleviation : 324,

Pensions : 329, 337
